boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Named, publicly documented destinations on campus-adjacent College Park corridors.

cards.title: City Hall Plaza for civic events
cards.subtitle: Baltimore Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Walk the Baltimore Avenue frontage and check the City calendar for an event at City Hall Plaza before you head over.
cards.short_summary: A public plaza at the City Hall and university shared building.
cards.evidence_claim: The City describes its City Hall building as a shared City–University space with a plaza fronting Baltimore Avenue.
cards.access_notes: Consult the City calendar for event-specific access.

cards.title: Old Parish House for preserved masonry
cards.subtitle: Knox Road corridor
cards.notes: Pause at 4711 Knox Road to view the restored historic exterior, then look up City arts programming scheduled there.
cards.short_summary: A restored historic building used for community programming.
cards.evidence_claim: The City identifies the Old Parish House at 4711 Knox Road and reports that its exterior historic masonry restoration was completed in late summer 2022.
cards.access_notes: Exterior viewing is the reliable option; program and building access vary.

cards.title: College Park Aviation Museum for aircraft exhibits
cards.subtitle: Campus Drive corridor
cards.notes: Follow Campus Drive toward Corporal Frank Scott Drive and use the museum’s current exhibit listing to plan a daytime visit.
cards.short_summary: An aviation museum at College Park Airport with full-size aircraft displays.
cards.evidence_claim: The museum has an exhibit area highlighting ten unique aircraft and early-aviation objects, and is located at 1985 Corporal Frank Scott Drive.
cards.access_notes: Listed hours are Tuesday–Sunday, 10 a.m.–4 p.m.; verify before visiting.

cards.entity_name: Lake Artemesia Natural Area at Lakeland
cards.title: Lake Artemesia for the lakeside trail
cards.subtitle: 55th Avenue / Paint Branch Trail corridor
cards.notes: Use the 55th Avenue entrance for the hard-surface trail and lakeside setting; plan the outing during the listed dawn-to-dusk hours.
cards.short_summary: A nearly 87-acre natural area with a lake and trail access.
cards.evidence_claim: Prince George’s County lists Lake Artemesia Natural Area at Lakeland at 8200 55th Avenue with trail access and dawn-to-dusk hours.
cards.source_title: Lake Artemesia Natural Area at Lakeland
cards.access_notes: Listed hours are dawn to dusk.

cards.title: Trolley Trail Arts Project for murals
cards.subtitle: Rhode Island Avenue / Trolley Trail corridor
cards.notes: Walk the northern Rhode Island Avenue Trolley Trail segment between Amherst Road and Greenbelt Road to find the installed murals.
cards.short_summary: A four-mural public-art installation along the Trolley Trail.
cards.evidence_claim: The City says four murals have been installed on the northern Trolley Trail between Amherst Road and Greenbelt Road.
cards.access_notes: Use the trail as a pedestrian or bicycle route and observe posted conditions.

cards.title: Paint Branch Trail for trail connections
cards.subtitle: Paint Branch Parkway corridor
cards.notes: Start near the Paint Branch Parkway corridor and use the City trail map to choose a connection toward Lake Artemesia or Cherry Hill.
cards.short_summary: A city-documented trail linking Lake Artemesia with Cherry Hill Neighborhood Park.
cards.evidence_claim: The City states that Paint Branch Trail runs between Cherry Hill Neighborhood Park and Lake Artemesia and connects with other regional trails.
cards.access_notes: Check trail conditions and daylight before setting out.

cards.title: Acredale Community Park for open-air recreation
cards.subtitle: Odessa Road corridor
cards.notes: Head to the 5300 block of Odessa Road for the named park and confirm current recreation conditions before planning a group stop.
cards.short_summary: A named College Park park and dog-park destination.
cards.evidence_claim: College Park’s parks page lists Acredale Community Park (and Dog Park) in the 5300 block of Odessa Road.
cards.access_notes: City parks close at dark, according to the City’s parks page.

cards.title: Hollywood Playground for a neighborhood event stop
cards.subtitle: Rhode Island Avenue / Hollywood corridor
cards.notes: Use the Rhode Island Avenue-side Hollywood corridor as your approach, then check the City calendar for any playground-based public programming.
cards.short_summary: A named playground used as a City calendar location.
cards.evidence_claim: The City’s public calendar identifies Hollywood Playground as the location for a neighborhood game night.
cards.access_notes: Check the City calendar for event dates and any access details.

cards.title: Calvert Park for City-run outdoor events
cards.subtitle: Calvert Road corridor
cards.notes: Approach from the Calvert Road corridor and look at the City calendar before visiting, especially if you are going for a scheduled activity.
cards.short_summary: A named park that appears as a City event location.
cards.evidence_claim: The City calendar lists Calvert Park as the location for its Egg Hunt EGG-STRAVAGANZA event.
cards.source_title: City of College Park calendar, March 2026
cards.access_notes: Check the City calendar for event-specific timing and access.

cards.title: The Mews Playground for a named local park stop
cards.subtitle: Catawba Street / 48th Place corridor
cards.notes: Use Catawba Street and 48th Place to locate this named playground, and keep the visit to daytime because City parks close at dark.
cards.short_summary: A City-listed playground at a named local-street junction.
cards.evidence_claim: College Park’s parks page lists The Mews Playground at Catawba Street and 48th Place.
cards.access_notes: City parks close at dark, according to the City’s parks page.
